### Definition and Usage

**AETERM** captures the **verbatim name of the adverse event** exactly as reported/collected. It is the **topic variable** for the AE dataset and is a **required variable** — it must always have a value.

### Key Business Rules

- **AETERM** holds the original verbatim term as collected; it is **not modified** for coding purposes.

- The dictionary-coded (standardized) term is derived into **AEDECOD** (Preferred Term from MedDRA), which is also a required variable.

[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_2]  
[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.3.6 Storing Topic Variables for General Domain Models]

---

### Relationship to Other Coding Variables

| Variable | Role | Content |
|----------|------|---------|
| AETERM | Topic | Original verbatim term as reported |
| AEMODIFY | Synonym Qualifier | Modified verbatim term (if applicable) |
| AEDECOD | Synonym Qualifier | Dictionary-derived Preferred Term (MedDRA) |

[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.3.6]

results.answer:
# Key Assumptions for Adverse Event Data Collection and Coding

## 1. Scope of AE Collection

The AE dataset includes "any untoward medical occurrence in a patient or clinical investigation subject administered a pharmaceutical product and which does not necessarily have to have a causal relationship with this treatment" (ICH E2A). Sponsors may extend or limit the scope in consultation with regulatory authorities, and the events included should be consistent with protocol requirements. Adverse events may be captured either as **free text** or via a **prespecified list of terms**. [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_1]

---

## 2. AE Description and Coding

| Variable | Role | Key Rule |
|----------|------|----------|
| AETERM | Topic | Verbatim term as collected; **required**, must have a value |
| AEMODIFY | Permissible | Included if sponsor permits modification of verbatim term for coding |
| AEDECOD | Required | Preferred term derived from coding dictionary (e.g., MedDRA); **must have a value** |
| AEBODSYS | Expected | System Organ Class (SOC) from coding dictionary; may differ from primary SOC |

The sponsor must provide the dictionary name and version used for coding via the external codelist element in the Define-XML document. [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_2]

---

## 3. Prespecified Terms and Presence/Absence of Events

- **AEPRESP = "Y"** indicates the event in AETERM was prespecified on the CRF. [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_4]
- If it is important to capture which prespecified events were **not** reported, those data should be submitted in a Findings class dataset (e.g., FA domain), with corresponding AE records having AEPRESP = "Y". [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_4]
- When both prespecified and free-text events are collected: AEPRESP = "Y" for prespecified events; **null** for free-text events. [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_4]
- For subjects with no adverse events, **do not** include a record in the AE submission dataset to indicate "no events." [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_4]

---

## 4. Other Qualifier Variables

- **Seriousness categories** (e.g., AESCAN, AESCONG, AESDTH, AESHOSP): If collected secondarily to a leading "Serious?" question, these may be null when AESER = "N". If "Serious?" = "Y", at least one must have a "Y" response. [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_7]
- **AESCAN** (Involves cancer) and **AESOD** (Occurred with overdose) are not part of the ICH definition of a serious AE but are available for studies under pre-ICH guidelines. [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_7]
- **AETOXGR** should be used instead of AESEV when a standard toxicity scale (e.g., NCI CTCAE) is used. In most cases, either AESEV or AETOXGR is populated, but not both. [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_7]
- Descriptions of "Other Medically Important Serious AE" should be placed in SUPPAE using the standard QNAM code **AEOSOSP**. [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_7]

---

## 5. Dataset Structure (One Record per Event)

The AE domain is structured as **1 record per adverse event per subject**. It is the sponsor's responsibility to define an "event." Common approaches include:

- **Collapsed summary records**: Multiple investigator-reported records submitted as 1 record with the highest severity, causality, seriousness, and final outcome.
- **Separate records for changes**: New records submitted when severity, causality, or seriousness changes or worsens (each treated as a distinct event). Changes over time may alternatively be submitted in an FA dataset.
- The submission dataset structure may differ from the collection structure (e.g., visit-level collection collapsed to event-level submission).

[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_7]

---

## 6. EPOCH and TAETORD

When EPOCH is included in the AE domain, it should reflect the epoch of the **start** of the adverse event (based on AESTDTC, not AEENDTC). Similarly, TAETORD should reflect the value for the start of the adverse event. The Define-XML computational method should describe assumptions for handling ambiguous cases (e.g., when AESTDTC and SESTDTC lack sufficient precision). [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_8]

---

## 7. Relationship to Other Domains

- When an AE leads to study discontinuation, the relationship between the AE record and the DS record should be represented in **RELREC**. [Source: domains/DS/examples.md -- Example 4]
- Visit-level severity assessments that do not describe the event as a whole should be placed in the **FA domain** (Findings About Events or Interventions), with FAOBJ populated with the value from AEDECOD. [Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md -- item_6; domains/FA/examples.md -- Example 6]
- Prespecified AE occurrence indicators at each visit are also represented in the **FA domain** (FATESTCD = OCCUR), with corresponding AE records having AEPRESP = "Y". [Source: domains/FA/examples.md -- Example 4]

results.answer:
# TV (Trial Visits) Domain

## Purpose

The TV domain describes the **protocol-defined planned schedule of subject encounters** (clinical encounters) at the healthcare facility where the study is being conducted. It provides the planned visit schedule to which a subject's actual visits can be compared.

Specifically, TV:
- Defines planned visits for the trial (as referenced by the SV domain for actual visits)
- Allows reviewers to compare planned vs. actual visit timing
- Supports identification of planned but not completed visits
- Describes visit start/end rules relative to trial elements and epochs

[Source: domains/TV/assumptions.md -- overview]  
[Source: domains/SV/assumptions.md -- item_1]

---

## Structure

**One Record per Planned Visit per Arm** (or one record per planned visit if the visit schedule is identical across all arms — in which case ARMCD is left blank).

[Source: domains/TV/assumptions.md -- item_1]

---

## Variables

Based on the retrieved context, the TV domain contains the following confirmed variables:

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core | Controlled Terms |
|----------|-------|------|------|------|-----------------|
| STUDYID | (Study Identifier) | — | Identifier | — | — |
| DOMAIN | (Domain Abbreviation) | — | Identifier | — | — |
| VISITNUM | Visit Number | Numeric | Timing | — | — |
| VISIT | Visit Name | Char | Synonym Qualifier | Req | — |
| VISITDY | Planned Study Day of Visit | — | Timing | — | — |
| ARMCD | Planned Arm Code | — | — | — | — |
| ARM | Description of Planned Arm | — | — | — | — |
| TVSTRL | Visit Start Rule | Char | Rule | Req | — |
| TVENRL | Visit End Rule | Char | Rule | Perm | — |

[Source: domains/TV/spec.md -- VISIT]  
[Source: domains/TV/spec.md -- TVSTRL]  
[Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- TV — Trial Visits (Trial Design)]

> **Note:** The full variable list with all Orders and CDISC Notes is in `domains/TV/spec.md`. The table above reflects variables confirmed in the retrieved context; additional variables (e.g., ARMCD, ARM, VISITDY) are referenced in assumptions and examples but their full spec rows were not retrieved.

---

## Key Implementation Notes

1. **VISIT, VISITNUM, VISITDY** are the three timing variables used to describe clinical encounters. There must be a **one-to-one relationship** between VISIT and VISITNUM. [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.5]

2. **TVSTRL** (Visit Start Rule) is **Required** and describes when the visit starts relative to the sequence of elements/epochs (e.g., *"1 week after start of Treatment Epoch"*). [Source: domains/TV/spec.md -- TVSTRL]

3. **TVENRL** (Visit End Rule) is **Permitted** and describes when the visit ends. [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- TV]

4. **Visit start rules** differ from element start rules — they describe *when* a visit should occur, not the moment it starts. Gaps between visits are normal. [Source: domains/TV/examples.md -- Trial Visits Issues]

5. **Contingent visits** (triggered by disease milestones or events) may be included in TV with a rule describing the circumstances under which they occur. [Source: domains/TV/examples.md -- Trial Visits Issues]

6. **Visit schedules may use ranges** (e.g., "12–16 days after start of 2nd Element"), which are distinct from analysis windows. [Source: domains/TV/examples.md -- Trial Visits Issues]

---

## Related Domains

| Domain | Relationship |
|--------|-------------|
| TA | Visits reference arms |
| SE | Planned visits vs. actual subject elements |
| SV | Actual subject visit timing (compared against TV planned visits) |
| TD, TM, TS, TE, TI | Same Trial Design class |

[Source: domains/TV/spec.md -- Related Domains]

# PE Domain — Dataset Structure, PETESTCD Role, and Special Value

## 1. Dataset Structure

The PE domain belongs to the **Findings** class and captures findings from physical examinations. Its natural key structure is one record per body system examined per subject per visit. Key variables include:

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core |
|----------|-------|------|------|------|
| PESEQ | Sequence Number | Num | Identifier | Req |
| PETESTCD | Body System Examined Short Name | Char | Topic | Req |
| PETEST | Body System Examined | Char | Synonym Qualifier | Req |
| PEORRES | Verbatim Examination Finding | Char | Result Qualifier | Exp |
| PESTRESC | Character Result/Finding in Std Format | Char | Result Qualifier | Exp |
| PEDTC | Date/Time of Examination | Char | Timing | Exp |

[Source: domains/PE/spec.md] [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md]

---

## 2. PETESTCD Variable Definition

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Label** | Body System Examined Short Name |
| **Type** | Char |
| **Role** | **Topic** |
| **Core** | Req |
| **Controlled Terms** | *(no codelist assigned; sponsor-defined)* |

**CDISC Notes constraints:**
- Cannot be longer than **8 characters**
- Cannot **start with a number** (e.g., "1TEST" is invalid)
- Cannot contain characters other than **letters, numbers, or underscores**
- Examples: `"HEAD"`, `"ENT"`

[Source: domains/PE/spec.md — PETESTCD]

---

## 3. Special Value When Entire Examination Is One Record

When the results of the **entire physical examination** are represented in a **single record**, PETESTCD must be set to:

> **`"PHYSEXAM"`**

Correspondingly, its long-name companion variable PETEST should be populated as:

> **`"Physical Examination"`**

[Source: domains/PE/spec.md — PETESTCD] [Source: domains/PE/spec.md — PETEST]

---

## 4. Practical Illustration

From the PE domain example, the typical multi-record approach looks like:

| PESEQ | PETESTCD | PETEST | PEORRES | PESTRESC |
|-------|----------|--------|---------|----------|
| 1 | HEAD | Head | NORMAL | NORMAL |
| 2 | ENT | Ear/Nose/Throat | NORMAL | NORMAL |
| 3 | SKIN | Skin | ACNE | Acne |
| 6 | HEART | Heart | NORMAL | NORMAL |

In contrast, if the sponsor chooses to collapse all findings into one record, PETESTCD = `"PHYSEXAM"` and PETEST = `"Physical Examination"` would be used instead.

[Source: domains/PE/examples.md — Example 1]

# LBTESTCD in the LB Domain

## Variable Definition

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Label** | Lab Test or Examination Short Name |
| **Type** | Char |
| **Role** | Topic |
| **Core** | Req |
| **Controlled Terms** | C65047 (Laboratory Test Code) |

[Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBTESTCD]

---

## Role

LBTESTCD serves as the **Topic variable** in the LB domain — it specifies the focus of the observation (i.e., the identity of the laboratory test or examination being performed). As a Topic variable, it is the primary descriptor around which all other qualifiers, result values, and timing variables are organized.

[Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBTESTCD]

---

## Controlled Terminology

LBTESTCD uses codelist **C65047** (Laboratory Test Code). This codelist contains standardized short names for laboratory tests. Examples of valid values from this codelist include:

- `KIM1S` — Soluble Kidney Injury Molecule-1
- `LACTICAC` — Lactic Acid
- `LAP` — Leucine Aminopeptidase
- `KLCFR` — Kappa Light Chain, Free

[Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- Controlled Terminology]  
[Source: terminology/core/lb_part2.md]

---

## Naming Constraints

LBTESTCD is subject to three strict formatting rules:

1. **Length**: The value cannot be longer than **8 characters**.
2. **Starting character**: The value **cannot start with a number** (e.g., `"1TEST"` is not valid).
3. **Allowed characters**: The value **cannot contain characters other than letters, numbers, or underscores**.

These constraints exist because LBTESTCD can be used as a **column name** when converting a dataset from vertical to horizontal (transposed) format.

[Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBTESTCD]

---

## Relationship to LBTEST

LBTESTCD is paired with **LBTEST** (Lab Test or Examination Name, codelist C67154), which holds the full verbatim name of the test (up to 40 characters, e.g., `"Alanine Aminotransferase"`). LBTEST carries the Role of **Synonym Qualifier** relative to LBTESTCD.

[Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBTEST]

---

## Special Usage: Tests Not Done

When an entire group of tests was not performed, LBTESTCD should be set to `"LBALL"` (with LBTEST = `"Laboratory Test Results"` and LBSTAT = `"NOT DONE"`), representing all tests in a given category.

[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.5.1 Original and Standardized Results]

# VS (Vital Signs) Domain

## Overview

The VS domain belongs to the **Findings** observation class and captures vital signs measurements collected during a clinical study. It is one of the most commonly submitted safety domains in regulatory submissions.

[Source: chapters/ch03_submitting_data.md]

---

## Key Variables

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core | CT |
|----------|-------|------|------|------|----|
| VSTESTCD | Vital Signs Test Short Name | Char | Topic | Req | C66741 |
| VSTEST | Vital Signs Test Name | Char | Synonym Qualifier | Req | C67153 |
| VSORRES | Result or Finding in Original Units | Char | Result Qualifier | Exp | — |
| VSORRESU | Original Units | Char | Variable Qualifier | Exp | C66770 |
| VSSTRESC | Character Result/Finding in Std Format | Char | Result Qualifier | Exp | — |
| VSSTRESN | Numeric Result/Finding in Standard Units | Num | Result Qualifier | Exp | — |
| VSSTRESU | Standard Units | Char | Variable Qualifier | Exp | C66770 |
| VSSTAT | Completion Status | Char | Record Qualifier | Perm | C66789 |
| VSPOS | Vital Signs Position of Subject | Char | Record Qualifier | Perm | C71148 |
| VSLOC | Location of Vital Signs Measurement | Char | Record Qualifier | Perm | C74456 |

[Source: domains/VS/spec.md, VARIABLE_INDEX.md]

---

## VSTESTCD — Vital Signs Test Short Name

- **Codelist:** C66741 (Vital Signs Test Code)
- **Paired with:** VSTEST (C67153, Vital Signs Test Name)
- **Constraints:** ≤ 8 characters, must not start with a number, letters/numbers/underscores only

**Examples provided in the CDISC Notes:**

| VSTESTCD | VSTEST |
|----------|--------|
| SYSBP | Systolic Blood Pressure |
| DIABP | Diastolic Blood Pressure |
| BMI | Body Mass Index |

[Source: domains/VS/spec.md — VSTESTCD, VSTEST]

> **Note:** The full list of allowed VSTESTCD values is defined in codelist **C66741**. The individual value codes within C66741 must be confirmed in the CDISC terminology file (`terminology/core/vs.md`); only the value names above are shown in the retrieved context.

---

## Units (VSORRESU / VSSTRESU) — Codelist C66770

This codelist is **extensible**. Examples of standard units include:

| Submission Value | Description |
|-----------------|-------------|
| `beats/min` | Beats per Minute (e.g., heart rate) |
| `breaths/min` | Breaths per Minute (e.g., respiratory rate) |
| `C` | Degree Celsius (e.g., temperature) |
| `F` | Degree Fahrenheit |
| `mmHg` | Millimeter of Mercury (e.g., blood pressure) |
| `kg` | Kilogram (e.g., body weight) |
| `kg/m2` | Kilogram per Square Meter (e.g., BMI) |
| `cm` | Centimeter (e.g., height) |
| `%` | Percentage (e.g., oxygen saturation) |

[Source: terminology/core/vs.md — Units for Vital Signs Results (C66770)]

---

## Additional Notes

- Reference ranges can be represented using `VSORNRLO`, `VSORNRHI`, and `VSNRIND` (from the Findings observation class). [Source: domains/VS/assumptions.md — item_2]
- Toxicity grading is captured in `VSTOX` and `VSTOXGR`. [Source: domains/VS/assumptions.md — item_2]
- Clinical significance is captured in `VSCLSIG` (codelist C66742, No Yes Response). [Source: domains/VS/spec.md]
- When a vital sign was not performed, `VSSTAT = "NOT DONE"` (codelist C66789) and `VSORRES`/`VSSTRESC`/`VSSTRESN` must all be null. [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.5.1]
- Associations between specific vital sign tests and qualifier codelists are described in the VS codetable at the CDISC terminology site. [Source: domains/VS/assumptions.md — item_3]

---

### Observation Class

The CM domain belongs to the **Interventions** observation class.

> "An interventions domain that contains concomitant and prior medications used by the subject, such as those given on an as needed basis or condition-appropriate medications." [Source: domains/CM/assumptions.md]

The dataset descriptor confirms this: `cm.xpt, Concomitant/Prior Medications — **Interventions**. One record per recorded intervention occurrence or constant-dosing interval per subject, Tabulation.` [Source: domains/CM/assumptions.md]

# MH Domain: MHTERM Role and Data Collection Assumptions

## MHTERM Variable Definition

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Label** | Reported Term for the Medical History |
| **Type** | Char |
| **Role** | Topic |
| **Core** | Req |
| **Controlled Terms** | *(none)* |

MHTERM captures the verbatim or preprinted CRF term for the medical condition or event. As the **Topic** variable, it is the primary subject of each MH record and is **required** — it must always have a value.

[Source: domains/MH/spec.md -- MHTERM]

---

## Domain Overview

MH is an **Events** domain containing data on a subject's prior medical history at the start of the trial.

[Source: domains/MH/assumptions.md -- overview]

---

## Key Assumptions Governing MH Data Collection

### 1. Description and Coding (Assumption 2)

- **MHTERM** is the topic variable capturing either the verbatim term collected or the prespecified term used to solicit occurrence of conditions. It is required and must have a value.
- **MHMODIFY** is permissible; include it if the sponsor's procedure permits modification of a verbatim term for coding purposes.
- **MHDECOD** is populated with the preferred term from a standard dictionary when the sponsor codes MHTERM. The dictionary name and version must be provided via the external codelist element in Define-XML.
- **MHBODSYS** represents the System Organ Class (SOC) from the coding dictionary. It may differ from the primary SOC in the dictionary's standard hierarchy, and is expected to be populated.
- When a CRF collects history by prespecified body systems **and** the sponsor codes using a dictionary, MHDECOD/MHBODSYS come from the dictionary, while **MHCAT/MHSCAT** represent the prespecified body systems.

[Source: domains/MH/assumptions.md -- item_2]

---

### 2. Categorization and Grouping (Assumption 3)

- **MHCAT** and **MHSCAT** may be populated with the sponsor's predefined categorization (often prespecified on the CRF).
  - MHCAT should **not** group all MH records into one generic label (e.g., "Medical History") — that is redundant with the domain code. If no smaller categorization applies, omit the variable.
  - Example valid MHCAT values: "GENERAL MEDICAL HISTORY", "ALLERGY MEDICAL HISTORY", "REPRODUCTIVE MEDICAL HISTORY" (with multiple distinct categories present).
- **MHGRPID** links related records at the subject level within MH (e.g., grouping syndromes related to a particular disease). It is **not** a substitute for MHCAT/MHSCAT, which group data across subjects.

[Source: domains/MH/assumptions.md -- item_3]

---

### 3. Prespecified Terms and Presence/Absence of Events (Assumption 4)

Medical history is collected in two ways — **free text** or **prespecified lists** — and the collection method must be reflected in the data:

| Situation | MHPRESP | MHOCCUR | MHSTAT |
|-----------|---------|---------|--------|
| Spontaneously reported event occurred | *(null)* | *(null)* | *(null)* |
| Pre-specified event occurred | Y | Y | *(null)* |
| Pre-specified event did not occur | Y | N | *(null)* |
| Pre-specified event has no response | Y | *(null)* | NOT DONE |

Key rules:
- **MHPRESP = "Y"** indicates the term was prespecified on the CRF.
- **MHOCCUR** (CT: C66742) indicates whether the prespecified condition occurred ("Y"/"N"). Values are **null** for spontaneously reported events.
- If all events were collected as free text, MHPRESP and MHOCCUR should be null and may be omitted from the dataset entirely.
- **MHSTAT** and **MHREASND** document prespecified questions for which no response was collected (MHSTAT = "NOT DONE"). These variables may be omitted if all events were free text or all prespecified conditions have responses in MHOCCUR.
- When free-text collection yields a "no medical history" entry for a subject or body system, **do not** include a record in MH to indicate no events.

[Source: domains/MH/assumptions.md -- item_4]

---

## Practical Illustration

From Example 2, the interaction of these variables is visible:

- Rows 1–3: Free-text General Medical History → MHPRESP and MHOCCUR are **null**; MHSCAT holds the body system; MHENRF reflects "ongoing at study start."
- Rows 5–8: Risk Factors CRF (prespecified) → MHPRESP = "Y"; MHOCCUR = "Y" or "N" per subject response.

[Source: domains/MH/examples.md -- Example 2]

## EGTESTCD — Detailed Specification

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Order** | 10 |
| **Label** | ECG Test or Examination Short Name |
| **Type** | Char |

| **Core** | Req |

**CDISC Notes:** Short name of the measurement, test, or examination described in EGTEST. It can be used as a column name when converting a dataset from a vertical to a horizontal format. The value in EGTESTCD:
- Cannot be longer than **8 characters**
- Cannot start with a number (e.g., "1TEST" is not valid)
- Cannot contain characters other than **letters, numbers, or underscores**
- Examples: `"PRAG"`, `"QRSAG"`

> **Key design note:** Test codes are in **2 separate codelists** — one for tests based on regular 10-second ECGs (codelist C71153, paired with EGTEST codelist C71152) and one for tests based on Holter monitoring (codelist C120523, paired with EGTEST codelist C120524).

[Source: domains/EG/spec.md — EGTESTCD; domains/EG/assumptions.md — item_2]

---

## Controlled Terminology Codelists for EGTESTCD

### C71153 — ECG Test Code
Used for standard 10-second ECG tests. Examples of values from this codelist include test codes such as `EGHRMN` (ECG Mean Heart Rate), `PRAG` (PR Interval, Aggregate), `QRSAG` (QRS Duration, Aggregate), `QTAG` (QT Interval, Aggregate), `QTCBAG`, `QTCFAG`, `INTP` (Interpretation), `TECHQUAL` (Technical Quality), etc. This codelist is **extensible**. [Source: domains/EG/examples.md — Example 1; domains/EG/spec.md]

### C120523 — Holter ECG Test Code
Used for tests based on Holter monitoring. This codelist is **extensible** and includes the following values:

| CDISC Submission Value | CDISC Synonym | Definition |
|------------------------|---------------|------------|
| AVCOND | Atrioventricular Conduction | ECG assessment of cardiac atrioventricular conduction |
| AXISVOLT | Axis and Voltage | Assessment of mean cardiac electrical vector and ECG voltage |
| CHYPTENL | Chamber Hypertrophy or Enlargement | ECG assessment of chamber hypertrophy or enlargement |
| EGCOMP | Comparison to a Prior ECG | Comparative interpretation relative to a previous ECG |
| INTP | Interpretation | Elucidation/explanation of the meaning of the event |
| IVTIACD | Intraventricular-Intraatrial Conduction | Assessment of intraventricular and intra-atrial conduction |
| MI | Myocardial Infarction | ECG assessment of findings suggestive of myocardial infarction |
| PACEMAKR | Pacemaker | ECG assessment of presence of artificial electronic pacing |
| RHYNOS | Rhythm Not Otherwise Specified | ECG assessment of cardiac rhythm NOS |
| SNRARRY | Sinus Node Rhythms and Arrhythmias | Assessment of sinus node rhythms and arrhythmias |
| SPRARRY | Supraventricular Arrhythmias | Assessment of supraventricular arrhythmias (excl. tachycardias) |
| SPRTARRY | Supraventricular Tachyarrhythmias | Assessment of supraventricular tachyarrhythmias |
| STSTWUW | ST Segment, T wave, and U wave | Assessment of ST segment, T wave, and U wave characteristics |
| TECHQUAL | Technical Quality | Statement about ECG recording describing technical issues |
| VTARRY | Ventricular Arrhythmias | Assessment of ventricular arrhythmias (excl. tachycardias) |
| VTTARRY | Ventricular Tachyarrhythmias | Assessment of ventricular tachyarrhythmias |

[Source: terminology/core/eg_part3.md — Holter ECG Test Code (C120523)]

---

## Key Design Notes

1. **Two-codelist architecture**: The split between C71153 (standard ECG) and C120523 (Holter) mirrors the same split for EGTEST (C71152 and C120524 respectively). [Source: domains/EG/spec.md — EGTEST; domains/EG/assumptions.md — item_2]

2. **EGCAT usage**: EGCAT (no controlled terminology) is used to group ECG observations, with sponsor-defined values such as `"MEASUREMENT"`, `"FINDING"`, `"INTERVAL"`. [Source: domains/EG/spec.md — EGCAT]

3. **Holter linkage**: When Holter monitoring data is collected, the PR domain records the procedure, EG records the findings, and RELREC links them via `--LNKID`. [Source: domains/PR/examples.md — Example 2]

4. **QT correction models**: When used with a QT correction model domain, EGTESTCD/EGTEST values are assigned at the study level with clear documentation (e.g., `QTCIAG1`, `QTCIAG2` for ranked best-fit models). [Source: domains/EG/assumptions.md — item_10]

results.answer:
# SUPPQUAL — Supplemental Qualifiers

## What is SUPPQUAL?

SUPPQUAL (Supplemental Qualifiers) is a **Relationship-class** dataset structure used to capture non-standard variables (NSVs) that cannot be accommodated within standard SDTM domain datasets. [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md]

The SDTM model does not allow the addition of new variables to standard domains. Therefore, the SUPP-- dataset model provides the mechanism for capturing sponsor-defined variables and associating them with parent records. [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.1]

### Dataset Naming Convention

There is a **one-to-one correspondence** between a domain dataset and its Supplemental Qualifier dataset, named `SUPP--` where `--` denotes the source domain:

- `suppae.xpt` → supplemental qualifiers for AE
- `suppdm.xpt` → supplemental qualifiers for DM
- `suppfamh.xpt` → for split domains (longer names permitted)
- `SQAPFAMH` → special case: when "SUPP" prefix would make the name too long (Associated Persons), shorten to "SQ"

The single SUPPQUAL dataset option introduced in SDTMIGv3.1 was **deprecated**. [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.2]

---

## SUPP-- Dataset Structure

The dataset contains 13 variables (per the SDTM v2.0 model): [Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md]

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core |
|----------|-------|------|------|------|
| STUDYID | Study Identifier | Char | Identifier | Req |
| RDOMAIN | Related Domain Abbreviation | Char | Identifier | Req |
| USUBJID | Unique Subject Identifier | Char | Identifier | Req |
| IDVAR | Identifying Variable | Char | Identifier | Exp |
| IDVARVAL | Identifying Variable Value | Char | Identifier | Exp |
| QNAM | Qualifier Variable Name | Char | Topic | Req |
| QLABEL | Qualifier Variable Label | Char | Synonym Qualifier | Req |
| QVAL | Data Value | Char | Result Qualifier | Req |
| QORIG | Origin | Char | Record Qualifier | Req |
| QEVAL | Evaluator | Char | Record Qualifier | Exp (CT: C78735) |

### Key Variable Rules

- **QNAM**: Max 8 characters; cannot start with a number; only letters, numbers, or underscores permitted [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/spec.md -- QNAM]
- **QVAL**: **Must never be null** — records with null QVAL must be deleted prior to submission [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- Key Rules]
- **QLABEL**: Max 40 characters [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.1]
- **QEVAL**: Null for objective/derived data; populated (e.g., "ADJUDICATION COMMITTEE", "SPONSOR") only for subjective attributions [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/spec.md -- QEVAL]

### Linking Back to Parent Records

A SUPP-- record links to its parent via **STUDYID + RDOMAIN + USUBJID + IDVAR/IDVARVAL**.

**Exception for DM**: Both IDVAR and IDVARVAL are null because STUDYID + RDOMAIN + USUBJID alone uniquely identify the DM record (one record per USUBJID). [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md]

### Uniqueness Constraint

The combined set of values for the first 6 columns (STUDYID through QNAM) must be **unique for every record**. If two evaluators provide the same type of determination, separate QNAM values must be used (e.g., `AETRTEMI` for investigator, `AETRTEMA` for adjudicator). [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md]

---

## When TO Use Supplemental Qualifiers

Use SUPP-- when:

1. **Sponsor-defined NSVs** need to be associated with parent records in Events, Findings, Interventions, DM, or SV domains [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md]
2. **Attributions** (subjective classifications/interpretations) from multiple evaluators are needed — e.g., an adjudication committee's assessment of an AE alongside the investigator's assessment in the standard domain [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.5.4]
3. **Secondary evaluations** of qualifier variables — primary evaluation goes in the standard domain; secondary evaluation goes in SUPP-- with QNAM formed by appending "1" to the standard variable name [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.5.4]
4. **Long text strings >200 characters** — overflow text is stored in sequential SUPP-- records (QNAM suffixed with 1, 2, etc.) [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.5.3]
5. A **QNAM value contributes to the natural key** of a domain record [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.1.9]

---

## When NOT to Use Supplemental Qualifiers

The following data should **not** be submitted as supplemental qualifiers: [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.4]

| Data Type | Correct Location |
|-----------|-----------------|
| Subject-level objective data (e.g., national origin, twin type) | SC domain |
| Findings interpretations that warrant a new test code/result | Additional --TESTCD record in the Findings domain (e.g., EGTESTCD = "INTP") |
| Free-text comments related to a record | CO special-purpose domain |
| Data not directly related to records in a parent domain | Separate general observation class or special-purpose domain |

---

## Summary

SUPP-- is the **only sanctioned mechanism** for extending SDTM domains with non-standard variables, because the SDTM model prohibits adding new columns to standard datasets. It should be used for genuine additional qualifiers of existing observations — not as a catch-all for any data that doesn't fit elsewhere. The key discipline is: if the data represents a **separate observation**, it belongs in its own domain; if it is a **qualifier of an existing observation** that has no standard variable, it belongs in SUPP--. [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md]

results.answer:
# EPOCH Variable in SDTM

## Purpose of EPOCH

EPOCH is a **Timing** variable used to associate an observation with a specific epoch (phase) of the study design. It links subject-level observations back to the trial design structure defined in the Trial Arms (TA) domain.

**Key guidance on how to assign EPOCH values:**

- For **Findings class** domains: EPOCH should be based on the **--DTC** variable (date/time of the test or specimen collection)
- For **Interventions or Events class** domains: EPOCH should be based on the **--STDTC** variable (start of the intervention or event)
- Sponsors should **not impute** EPOCH values, but may assign them based on CRF instructions/structure even when date/time precision is insufficient
- EPOCH should be **null** for observations that occurred before the subject's participation in the study (including pre-screening), and when the epoch cannot be determined

| **Label** | Epoch |
| **Type** | Char |
| **Role** | Timing |
| **Core** | Perm |
| **Controlled Terms** | C99079 |

Example values: "SCREENING", "TREATMENT", "FOLLOW-UP"

[Source: domains/SR/spec.md]  
[Source: domains/CP/spec.md]  
[Source: domains/FA/spec.md]  
[Source: domains/PP/spec.md]  
[Source: domains/PC/spec.md]

> *"EPOCH may be used as a timing variable in other datasets, such as Exposure (EX) and Disposition (DS)"*

[Source: domains/TA/assumptions.md item_12]

EPOCH is a general Timing variable that is **permissible in any domain based on the three general observation classes** (Interventions, Events, Findings). The retrieved context confirms it is not applicable to:
- **SUPPQUAL** datasets
- **RELREC** datasets
- Observations that occurred **before the subject's study participation**

[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.3]

# USUBJID as a Linking Key Across SDTM Domains

## Definition

USUBJID is defined consistently across all domains as:

> **Unique Subject Identifier** — "Identifier used to uniquely identify a subject across all studies for all applications or submissions involving the product."

- **Type:** Char
- **Role:** Identifier
- **Core:** Req (in most domains; Exp in RELSUB where either USUBJID or POOLID must be populated)

[Source: domains/DM/spec.md, domains/AE/spec.md, domains/PP/spec.md, domains/CO/spec.md, domains/SUPPQUAL/spec.md, domains/RELSPEC/spec.md, domains/RELSUB/spec.md]

---

## How USUBJID Functions as a Linking Key

### 1. Primary Subject Identifier Across All Domains

USUBJID is the universal subject-level key that appears in every domain dataset. Because it is **Required** in virtually all domains, every observation record can be traced back to a specific subject. In DM, it may be constructed as a compound identifier: `STUDYID-SITEID-SUBJID`. [Source: domains/DM/spec.md]

### 2. Dataset-Level Metadata Keys

USUBJID is explicitly listed as a primary key component in the dataset-level metadata for all major domains:

| Dataset | Keys |
|---------|------|
| DM | STUDYID, USUBJID |
| SE | STUDYID, USUBJID, ETCD, SESTDTC |
| SM | STUDYID, USUBJID, MIDS |
| SV | STUDYID, USUBJID, SVTERM |
| AG | STUDYID, USUBJID, AGTRT, AGSTDTC |
| CO | STUDYID, USUBJID, IDVAR, COREF, COOTC |

[Source: chapters/ch03_submitting_data.md]

### 3. Linking Within RELREC (Record-Level Relationships)

In RELREC, USUBJID is used for **record-to-record** relationships (i.e., linking specific records within a subject). When RELREC is used for **dataset-to-dataset** relationships, USUBJID is intentionally **null** — because the relationship applies across all subjects, not to a single subject's record.

> "Note that because this is a dataset-to-dataset relationship, USUBJID and IDVARVAL are null."

[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md]

### 4. Linking Parent Records in SUPP-- Datasets

In Supplemental Qualifier datasets (SUPP--), USUBJID is one of the key variables used to identify the **parent record** to which a non-standard variable value belongs. This allows SUPP-- records to be joined back to their parent domain records. [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md]

### 5. Special Case: RELSUB (Related Subjects)

In RELSUB, USUBJID has Core = **Exp** (Expected) rather than Required, because either USUBJID or POOLID must be populated — accommodating pooled subject scenarios while still using USUBJID as the primary linking mechanism when individual subjects are referenced. [Source: domains/RELSUB/spec.md]

### 6. Associated Persons Domains

In AP (Associated Persons) domains, **APID** replaces USUBJID as the primary identifier. However, **RSUBJID** is used to link back to the USUBJID of the related study subject, preserving the cross-domain linkage to the subject-level data. [Source: model/04_associated_persons.md]

---

## Summary

USUBJID serves as the **universal subject-level foreign key** across the entire SDTM submission:

- It is **Required** in nearly every domain, ensuring every observation is attributable to a subject
- It forms part of the **natural key** (primary key) for dataset-level metadata
- It enables **record-to-record joins** in RELREC and SUPP-- relationship structures
- It is the reference point for AP domain linking via RSUBJID
- Its cross-study uniqueness (typically `STUDYID-SITEID-SUBJID`) supports integrated analyses across studies

results.answer:
# Linking Adverse Events to Concomitant Medications Using RELREC

## Overview

The RELREC dataset is used to represent **collected relationships** between AE records and CM records — for example, when a concomitant medication was taken specifically as a result of an adverse event. This relationship is typically captured via explicit CRF references or checkboxes.

[Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md]

---

## Step-by-Step Mechanism

### 1. Flag in AE Domain

The variable **AECONTRT** (Label: "Concomitant or Additional Trtmnt Given", Controlled Terms: C66742) is a Y/N Record Qualifier (Core: Perm) in the AE domain that indicates whether another treatment was given because of the event.

> If the non-study treatment is collected, the name and other information about the treatment should be represented in the appropriate Interventions domain — usually CM or PR — **and linked to the AE record with RELREC**.

[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_6]  
[Source: domains/AE/spec.md — AECONTRT]

### 2. Construct RELREC Records

For each relationship, one RELREC record is created **per participating record** (AE side and CM side), all sharing the same **RELID** value within a USUBJID.

Key variables used:

| Variable | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| STUDYID | Study identifier |
| RDOMAIN | Domain code of the record (e.g., `"AE"` or `"CM"`) |
| USUBJID | Subject identifier |
| IDVAR | Variable used to identify the record (e.g., `AESEQ`, `CMSEQ`, or `CMGRPID`) |
| IDVARVAL | Value of IDVAR for the specific record |
| RELID | Sponsor-assigned relationship identifier — **must be identical for all related records within USUBJID** |

[Source: domains/RELREC/spec.md — RELID]  
[Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md]

---

## Concrete Examples

### Example 1 — One AE linked to two CM records (via --SEQ)

AE record (AESEQ=5) is related to two CM records (CMSEQ=11 and CMSEQ=12):

| Row | STUDYID | RDOMAIN | USUBJID | IDVAR | IDVARVAL | RELTYPE | RELID |
|-----|---------|---------|---------|-------|----------|---------|-------|
| 1 | EFC1234 | AE | 123456 | AESEQ | 5 | | 1 |
| 2 | EFC1234 | CM | 123456 | CMSEQ | 11 | | 1 |
| 3 | EFC1234 | CM | 123456 | CMSEQ | 12 | | 1 |

[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md — 8.2.2 RELREC Dataset Examples]

### Example 2 — Using CMGRPID to reduce RELREC records

If the two CM records are already grouped in the CM domain using `CMGRPID = "COMBO1"`, the relationship can be expressed more efficiently with only **one CM-side RELREC record** pointing to the group:

| Row | STUDYID | RDOMAIN | USUBJID | IDVAR | IDVARVAL | RELTYPE | RELID |
|-----|---------|---------|---------|-------|----------|---------|-------|
| 1 | EFC1234 | AE | 123456 | AESEQ | 5 | | 1 |
| 2 | EFC1234 | CM | 123456 | CMGRPID | COMBO1 | | 1 |

[Source: domains/RELREC/examples.md — Example 3]  
[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md — 8.2.2 RELREC Dataset Examples]

---

## Key Rules

1. **RELID** must be unique within USUBJID and identical across all records in the same relationship. The sponsor chooses the value; a consistent naming convention (e.g., all numbers, all caps) is recommended. [Source: domains/RELREC/spec.md — RELID]

2. A single AE record can participate in **multiple relationships** (different RELID values), e.g., one relationship to CM records and another to LB records simultaneously. [Source: domains/RELREC/examples.md — Example 1]

3. **RELTYPE** is left null for peer-record relationships (it is only populated when relating datasets in a one-to-many sense). [Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md]

4. Using `--GRPID` in IDVAR (instead of `--SEQ`) is a more **efficient** method when multiple CM records form a combination therapy. [Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md]

# Linking TR and RS Domains in Oncology Studies

## Overview of the Multi-Domain Architecture

The oncology assessment data model uses three interconnected domains:
- **TU** (Tumor/Lesion Identification) — identifies and characterizes each tumor/lesion
- **TR** (Tumor/Lesion Results) — records measurements/assessments of identified tumors
- **RS** (Disease Response) — records overall response evaluations derived from TR (and potentially other domains)

[Source: domains/TR/assumptions.md -- overview]

---

## Linkage Direction 1: TU → TR (Identification to Results)

### Variable: `TRLNKID`

The `TRLNKID` variable in TR links each measurement/assessment record back to the corresponding identification record in TU.

> "The --LNKID variable is used for values that support a RELREC dataset-to-dataset relationship and to provide a unique code for each identified tumor/lesion/location of interest."

- A **dataset-to-dataset RELREC relationship** is the recommended linking mechanism
- `--GRPID`, `--REFID`, and `--SPID` cannot be used for this purpose as they may serve other functions per the SDTM
- The corresponding variable on the TU side is `TULNKID`, which carries compound values encoding: role/assessor, target vs. non-target status, tracking number, and split indicators

[Source: domains/TR/assumptions.md -- item_1]  
[Source: domains/TU/assumptions.md -- item_2]

---

## Linkage Direction 2: TR → RS (Results to Response Assessment)

### Variable: `TRLNKGRP`

The `TRLNKGRP` variable in TR links a **group** of TR records to a single response assessment record in RS.

> "TRLNKGRP is used to relate records in the TR domain to a response assessment record in the RS domain... The --LNKGRP variable is used for values that support a RELREC dataset-to-dataset relationship and to provide a unique code for each response and associated tumor/lesion measurements/assessments."

- Again, a **dataset-to-dataset RELREC relationship** is required
- `--GRPID`, `--REFID`, and `--SPID` are excluded for the same reason as above

[Source: domains/TR/assumptions.md -- item_2]

### Corresponding Variable on the RS Side: `RSLNKGRP`

On the RS side, `RSLNKGRP` provides the matching link back to the contributing TR records:

> "The RSLNKGRP variable is used to provide a link between the records in a findings domain (e.g., TR; LB) that contribute to a record in the RS domain. Records should exist in the RELREC dataset to support this relationship."

Additionally, `RSLNKID` can be used when a response evaluation relates back to a **specific source record** (e.g., a single tumor assessment in TR), as opposed to a group of records.

[Source: domains/RS/assumptions.md -- item_4]

---

## Important Scope Note: RS Is Not Limited to TR Data

The RS domain may incorporate data from domains **beyond TR**:

> "A set of oncology response criteria might require lab results in the LB domain, not only tumor results in the TR domain."

All source data must be represented in their topic-based domains (e.g., lab values in LB), and the RELREC linkage mechanism applies regardless of which domain the contributing data reside in.

[Source: domains/RS/assumptions.md -- item_4, item_5]

---

## Summary Table

| Linkage | Source Variable | Target Domain | Mechanism |
|---------|----------------|---------------|-----------|
| TU → TR | `TULNKID` (TU) / `TRLNKID` (TR) | TU ↔ TR | RELREC dataset-to-dataset |
| TR → RS (group) | `TRLNKGRP` (TR) / `RSLNKGRP` (RS) | TR ↔ RS | RELREC dataset-to-dataset |
| TR/other → RS (single record) | `RSLNKID` (RS) | TR or other → RS | RELREC record-to-record |

---

## Practical Example

In the RS examples, `RSLNKGRP = "A2"` on the Overall Response record (RSTESTCD = `OVRLRESP`) at WEEK 6 links back to the group of TR records that contributed to that overall assessment. Rows without `RSLNKGRP` populated (e.g., target response, non-target response) are component assessments that feed into the overall response but are not themselves the "group anchor."

[Source: domains/RS/examples.md -- RS — Examples - Disease Response]

results.answer:
# FA Domain: Findings About Events or Interventions

## Overview

The FA domain is a **Findings About** subtype of the Findings observation class. It is used to record findings *related to* observations in the Interventions or Events classes — specifically when those findings cannot be adequately captured as qualifiers on the parent record itself.

> "The Findings About observation class is a subtype of Findings used to record findings about events or interventions." [Source: model/02_observation_classes.md]

---

## When to Use FA (Three Criteria)

### Criterion 1 — Different Timing
Data or observations that have **different timing** from the associated event or intervention as a whole. For example, severity of an individual symptom assessed at multiple time points, while the AE record captures the event from start to finish.

### Criterion 2 — Multiple Variables Required
An observation about an event or intervention that **requires more than 1 variable** for its representation, preventing its inclusion as a single supplemental qualifier (e.g., a measurement with both a value and a unit).

### Criterion 3 — Pre-specified AE Occurrence
Data or information that **indicate the occurrence of pre-specified AEs** (e.g., solicited adverse events checked at each visit).

[Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md]

---

## The Key Linking Variable: FAOBJ

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core | CT |
|----------|-------|------|------|------|----|
| FAOBJ | Object of the Observation | Char | Record Qualifier | Req | — |

**FAOBJ** is the variable unique to the Findings About subtype. It identifies the **event or intervention that the measurement/evaluation is about**.

> "FATESTCD describes the measurement/evaluation and FAOBJ describes the event or intervention that the measurement/evaluation is about." [Source: model/02_observation_classes.md]

Both FATESTCD and FAOBJ are **required (Req)** on every FA record — together they fully define the topic of the observation. [Source: domains/FA/spec.md]

---

## How FA Links to Parent Domains

### Structural Relationship

FA does **not** use a foreign key variable pointing directly to the parent domain's sequence number. Instead, linkage is established through:

1. **FAOBJ** — populated with the name of the event or intervention (e.g., the value of AEDECOD from the AE domain)
2. **FASPID** — populated with the sponsor-defined identifier of the parent record (e.g., AESPID value), enabling traceability
3. **RELREC** — an optional formal relationship dataset that can explicitly link FA records to parent AE or CM records

[Source: domains/FA/examples.md — Example 2, Example 6]

### FA → AE Linkage Example

From Example 6, where severity of an AE is assessed at each visit:

**ae.xpt (parent)**
| AESEQ | AESPID | AETERM | AEDECOD | AESEV |
|-------|--------|--------|---------|-------|
| 1 | 1 | Morning queasiness | Nausea | MODERATE |

**faae.xpt (child)**
| FASEQ | FASPID | FATESTCD | FATEST | FAOBJ | FAORRES | FADTC |
|-------|--------|----------|--------|-------|---------|-------|
| 1 | 1 | SEV | Severity/Intensity | Nausea | MILD | 2006-02-02 |
| 2 | 1 | SEV | Severity/Intensity | Nausea | MODERATE | 2006-02-09 |

- **FAOBJ = "Nausea"** matches **AEDECOD = "Nausea"** in the parent AE record
- **FASPID = "1"** matches **AESPID = "1"** in the parent AE record

[Source: domains/FA/examples.md]

### FA → AE Linkage Example (Pre-specified AEs, Criterion 3)

**faae.xpt**
| FATESTCD | FATEST | FAOBJ | FAORRES |
|----------|--------|-------|---------|
| OCCUR | Occurrence Indicator | Headache | Y |
| OCCUR | Occurrence Indicator | Nausea | N |

For each prespecified AE where FAORRES = "Y", a corresponding AE record exists with **AEPRESP = "Y"**. [Source: domains/FA/examples.md — Example 4]

---

## Common FATESTCD Values in FA

When collected data fit a qualifier variable and are represented in FA, the variable name is used as FATESTCD:

| FATESTCD | FATEST |
|----------|--------|
| OCCUR | Occurrence Indicator |
| SEV | Severity/Intensity |
| TOXGR | Toxicity Grade |

[Source: model/02_observation_classes.md]

---

## Related Source Domains

FA can record findings about observations from multiple parent domains:

| Source Domain | Description |
|---------------|-------------|
| AE | Findings about adverse events |
| CM | Findings about concomitant medications |
| PR | Findings about procedures |
| EX | Findings about exposure |
| EC | Findings about exposure as collected |
| ML | Findings about meals |
| SU | Findings about substance use |

[Source: domains/FA/spec.md]

---

## Variables Generally NOT Used in FA

The following qualifiers should generally **not** be used in FA:
`--BODSYS`, `--MODIFY`, `--SEV`, `--TOXGR`

(Note: SEV and TOXGR are represented as FATESTCD values instead, not as separate qualifier columns.)

[Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md]

results.answer:
# How TA, TE, TV, and TI Work Together to Define a Study Design

These four Trial Design domains form a complementary framework: TE defines the **building blocks**, TA assembles them into **paths**, TV schedules **when assessments occur** along those paths, and TI specifies **who is eligible** to enter them.

---

## 1. TE — Trial Elements: The Building Blocks

TE defines the discrete, reusable time periods that constitute a trial.

> "An element is a building block for creating study cells, and an arm is composed of study cells."
> [Source: domains/TE/assumptions.md]

Each record in TE represents a **unique element** — analogous to a unique CRF page template. The same element may appear in multiple arms or multiple times within one arm, but it appears **only once** in TE.

Key variables [Source: model/05_study_level_data.md]:

| Variable | Role | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| ETCD | Topic | Unique element code |
| ELEMENT | Synonym Qualifier | Human-readable description |
| TESTRL | Rule | Condition for starting the element |
| TEENRL | Rule | Condition for ending the element |
| TEDUR | Timing | Planned duration |

---

## 2. TA — Trial Arms: Assembling Elements into Paths

TA takes the elements defined in TE and arranges them into **ordered sequences** (arms), one record per element per arm.

> "An arm is composed of elements; that is, the trial design assigns subjects to arms, which comprise a sequence of steps called elements."
> [Source: domains/TA/assumptions.md]

Key variables [Source: model/05_study_level_data.md]:

| Variable | Role | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| ARMCD / ARM | Topic / Synonym Qualifier | Identifies the arm |
| ETCD | Record Qualifier | References the element from TE |
| TAETORD | Timing | Order of the element within the arm |
| EPOCH | Timing | The epoch this element belongs to |
| TABRANCH | Rule | Fork condition (e.g., "Randomized to Arm A") |
| TATRANS | Rule | Within-arm transition condition (skip-ahead logic) |

The relationship is explicit: **TA references ETCD values defined in TE**, and the same ETCD can appear in multiple TA rows (multiple arms, or multiple positions within one arm). [Source: domains/TA/spec.md]

### Transition Logic Between Elements

The handoff between elements is a three-step process governed by both TE and TA:

| Step | Question | Answered by |
|------|----------|-------------|
| 1 | Should the subject leave the current element? | TEENRL in TE |
| 2 | Which element comes next (if a branch)? | TABRANCH in TA |
| 3 | Should the subject skip ahead? | TATRANS in TA |

[Source: domains/TE/examples.md]

---

## 3. TV — Trial Visits: Scheduling Assessments Along the Path

TV defines **when planned visits occur** relative to the epoch/element structure established by TA and TE.

> "Visits reference arms" and "planned visits vs actual subject elements" are the key cross-domain relationships.
> [Source: domains/TV/spec.md]

TV visit timing rules (TVSTRL / TVENRL) are expressed in terms of epoch or element start/end points — directly referencing the temporal landmarks created by TA and TE. For example:

| VISITNUM | TVSTRL | TVENRL |
|----------|--------|--------|
| 3 | 30 minutes before end of Run-in Epoch | 1 hour after start of Treatment Epoch |
| 4 | 1 week after start of Treatment Epoch | 1 hour after start of Visit |

[Source: domains/TV/examples.md]

**Important nuance:** When an arm includes repetitions of the same element, TAETORD (from TA) may need to be referenced alongside the element name to unambiguously anchor a visit. [Source: domains/TV/examples.md]

---

## 4. TI — Trial Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria: Defining Eligibility

TI operates at a different level — it is a **tabular synopsis of the protocol's eligibility criteria**, defining which subjects are permitted to enter the arms defined in TA.

> "TI contains all the inclusion and exclusion criteria for the trial, and thus provides information that may not be present in the subject-level data."
> [Source: domains/TI/assumptions.md]

TI complements the subject-level IE domain (Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria Not Met), which records only criteria that were **not met** by individual subjects. TI provides the complete planned criteria set against which IE records are interpreted.

---

## Integration Summary

```
TI  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────►
     Defines who is eligible to enter the trial

TE  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────►
     Defines unique time-period building blocks (ETCD, TESTRL, TEENRL, TEDUR)
                    │
                    ▼ (ETCD referenced by)
TA  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────►
     Assembles elements into ordered arm paths (TAETORD, EPOCH, TABRANCH, TATRANS)
                    │
                    ▼ (Epoch/Element landmarks referenced by)
TV  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────►
     Anchors planned visits to epoch/element transitions (TVSTRL, TVENRL)
```

Together, these four domains allow reviewers to:
- **Clearly and quickly grasp** the design of a clinical trial
- **Compare planned and actual** treatments and visits for subjects
- **Search a data warehouse** for trials with certain design features

[Source: domains/TA/assumptions.md]

- **Dataset name:** co.xpt
- **Purpose:** Captures comments that may be collected alongside other data — typically from a principal investigator, but also from central reviewers or other sources [Source: model/03_special_purpose_domains.md -- Comments (CO)]
- Comments are generally **not** responses to specific questions; they are voluntary free-text or unsolicited observations [Source: domains/CO/assumptions.md -- item_1]

---

## 2. Variable Specification

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core | CT |
|----------|-------|------|------|------|----|
| STUDYID | Study Identifier | Char | Identifier | Req | — |
| DOMAIN | Domain Abbreviation | Char | Identifier | Req | — |
| RDOMAIN | Related Domain Abbreviation | Char | Record Qualifier | — | C66734 |
| USUBJID | Unique Subject Identifier | Char | Identifier | Req | — |
| POOLID | Pool Identifier | Char | Identifier | Perm | — |
| COSEQ | Sequence Number | Num | Identifier | Req | — |
| IDVAR | Identifying Variable | Char | Record Qualifier | — | — |
| IDVARVAL | Identifying Variable Value | Char | Record Qualifier | — | — |
| COREF | Comment Reference | Char | Record Qualifier | Perm | — |
| COVAL | Comment | Char | Topic | Req | — |
| COEVAL | Evaluator | Char | Record Qualifier | Perm | C78735 |
| COEVALID | Evaluator Identifier | Char | Record Qualifier | Perm | C96777 |
| CODTC | Date/Time of Comment | Char | Timing | Perm | ISO 8601 |
| CODY | Study Day of Comment | Num | Timing | Perm | — |

[Source: model/03_special_purpose_domains.md -- Comments (CO); VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- CO]

---

## 3. The RDOMAIN / IDVAR / IDVARVAL Mechanism

CO uses the **same key structure as SUPP-- datasets** — specifically the variables RDOMAIN, IDVAR, and IDVARVAL — to identify the parent record(s) to which a comment relates. [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.5 Relating Comments to a Parent Domain]

### Three Scenarios for Populating These Keys

The CO domain accommodates three sources of comments, each with a different population pattern:

| Scenario | RDOMAIN | IDVAR | IDVARVAL | CODTC |
|----------|---------|-------|----------|-------|
| **a. Unrelated to any domain or record** (e.g., general comment log page) | null | null | null | Populate if captured |
| **b. Related to a domain, but not a specific record** (e.g., comment at bottom of PE CRF page) | Domain code (e.g., `"PE"`) | null | null | Populate if captured |
| **c. Related to specific parent record(s)** (e.g., comment about a specific AE) | Domain code (e.g., `"AE"`) | Key variable name (e.g., `"AESEQ"`) | Value of that key (e.g., `"7"`) | **null** — timing is inherited from parent |

[Source: domains/CO/assumptions.md -- item_3]

### Key Rules for Scenario (c)

- **RDOMAIN** is set to the 2-character DOMAIN code of the parent dataset (e.g., `"AE"`, `"EX"`, `"VS"`)
- **IDVAR** contains the **name** of the identifying variable in the parent domain (e.g., `AESEQ`, `EXGRPID`, `VSGRPID`)
- **IDVARVAL** contains the **value** of that variable for the specific parent record(s)
- **CODTC should be null** when the comment is linked to a specific record, because the timing is inherited from the parent record(s)
- Grouping variables (e.g., --GRPID) can be used in IDVAR to relate a comment to **multiple records** within one domain

[Source: domains/CO/assumptions.md -- item_3; chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.5]

### Limitation: Single Domain per CO Record

> "A single comment may only be related to a group of records in 1 domain (RDOMAIN can have only 1 value). If a single comment relates to records in multiple domains, the comment may need to be repeated in the CO special-purpose domain."

[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.5 Relating Comments to a Parent Domain]

---

## 4. Additional Referencing Mechanisms

Beyond RDOMAIN/IDVAR/IDVARVAL, two supplementary mechanisms exist:

- **COREF** — Free-text reference (e.g., CRF page number or visit name) for additional context that cannot be expressed via the key variables
- **Timing variables** (e.g., VISITNUM, VISIT) — May be added to CO to associate a comment with a particular visit

[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.5]

---

## 5. Long Comment Text

When comment text exceeds 200 characters:
- First 200 characters → **COVAL**
- Next 200 characters → **COVAL1**
- Additional text → **COVALn** (as needed)

[Source: domains/CO/assumptions.md -- item_4]

---

## 6. Concrete Example

From the CO examples dataset (co.xpt):

| Row | RDOMAIN | IDVAR | IDVARVAL | COREF | Description |
|-----|---------|-------|----------|-------|-------------|
| 1 | *(null)* | *(null)* | *(null)* | — | General comment, no domain link |
| 2 | `PE` | *(null)* | *(null)* | `VISIT 7` | Comment on PE domain, specific visit |
| 3 | `AE` | `AESEQ` | `7` | `PAGE 650` | Comment on single AE record |
| 4 | `EX` | `EXGRPID` | `COMBO1` | `PAGE 320-355` | Comment on group of EX records |
| 5 | `VS` | `VSGRPID` | `VS2` | — | Comment on group of VS records |

[Source: domains/CO/examples.md -- Example 1]

results.answer:
# EC vs. EX: Purpose Differences and Usage Guidance

## Core Distinction

| Dimension | EC (Exposure as Collected) | EX (Exposure) |
|-----------|---------------------------|---------------|
| **Nature** | Raw, as-collected data | Derived dataset |
| **Unit** | Product-level (e.g., tablets, mL) | Protocol-specified unit (e.g., mg, mg/kg) |
| **Perspective** | What was physically recorded/collected | What was actually administered in study terms |

---

## EC Domain Purpose

EC reflects **protocol-specified study treatment administrations, as collected** — i.e., the raw CRF data before any derivation or unit conversion.

**Use EC when collected exposure information cannot or should not be directly represented in EX**, for example:
- Administrations collected in **tablets** when the protocol-specified unit is **mg**
- Administrations collected in **mL** when the protocol-specified unit is **mg/kg**

EC is also used to capture:
- **ECMOOD = "SCHEDULED"** records (intended/planned doses)
- **ECMOOD = "PERFORMED"** records (actual administrations)
- Doses that were **not given** (ECOCCUR = "N" with ECREASOC explaining why)

> Note: Product accountability details (amount dispensed, amount returned) go in the **DA** domain, not EC. [Source: domains/EC/assumptions.md -- item_1]

---

## EX Domain Purpose

EX is **recognized in most cases as a derived dataset** where EXDOSU reflects the **protocol-specified unit** per study treatment. It is derived from collected data points (e.g., number of tablets, total volume infused) combined with additional inputs (e.g., randomization file, concentration, dosage strength, product accountability).

**EX is required for all studies that include protocol-specified study treatment.** [Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_1]

Common derivation methods (most to least direct):
1. Derived from actual observation of administration by the investigator
2. Derived from automated dispensing device
3. Derived from subject recall
4. Derived from product accountability data
5. Derived from the protocol

EX contains **1 record per constant-dosing interval per subject** and includes only treatments **received** (not missed/not given). [Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_1]

---

## When to Use Each

| Scenario | Use |
|----------|-----|
| Collected in tablets, protocol unit is mg | EC + EX |
| Collected in mL, protocol unit is mg/kg | EC + EX |
| Entire EC dataset would be an exact duplicate of EX | EC is **optional** (sponsor's discretion) |
| Intended/scheduled doses need to be captured | EC (with ECMOOD = "SCHEDULED") |
| Doses not administered | EC (ECOCCUR = "N") — no EX record |
| Protocol-specified unit directly matches collected unit | EX alone may suffice |

[Source: domains/EC/assumptions.md -- item_1]

---

## Relationship Between EC and EX

- The **degree of summarization** from EC to EX is sponsor-defined to support study purpose and analysis.
- When the relationship between EC and EX records can be described in **RELREC**, it should be defined.
- **EX derivations must be described in the Define-XML document.**

[Source: domains/EC/assumptions.md -- item_6] [Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_5]

---

## Practical Example

In Example 7 (weekly infusions of Drug Z 10 mg/kg):
- **EC** captured: intended dose in mg/kg (ECMOOD = "SCHEDULED"), actual volume in mL with concentration in mg/mL (ECMOOD = "PERFORMED"), and a missed dose (ECOCCUR = "N")
- **EX** captured: only the two actual administrations converted to mg/kg (protocol-specified unit); no record for the missed dose

[Source: domains/EX/examples.md -- Example 7]

---

## Special Note on EXVAMT/ECVAMT

When EC is implemented in conjunction with EX, **EXVAMT and EXVAMTU would not be used in EX**; collected values are instead represented in ECDOSE/ECDOSU (and ECVAMT/ECVAMTU as needed) in the EC domain. [Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_6]

results.answer:
# VISIT and VISITNUM Usage Across Observation-Class Domains, and the Role of SV

## 1. VISIT and VISITNUM in Observation-Class Domains

### Variable Definitions

VISITNUM and VISIT appear as **Timing** variables in all three general observation classes (Interventions, Events, Findings). For example:

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core |
|----------|-------|------|------|------|
| VISITNUM | Visit Number | Num | Timing | Exp |
| VISIT | Visit Name | Char | Timing | Perm |

[Source: domains/AG/spec.md -- VISITNUM], [Source: domains/FA/spec.md -- VISITNUM], [Source: domains/PE/spec.md -- VISITNUM]

### Consistency Rules for Planned Visits

For **planned visits**, values of VISIT, VISITNUM, and VISITDY **must** be those defined in the Trial Visits (TV) dataset:

- **VISITNUM**: Numeric, used for sorting; values should wherever possible match the planned chronological order of visits.
- **VISIT**: Character name of the visit from the protocol.
- **VISITDY**: The planned study day of the **start** of the visit (not the actual study day; do not use --DY).
- There must be a **one-to-one relationship** between VISIT and VISITNUM.

[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.5 Clinical Encounters and Visits]

The TV dataset is the authoritative source: values of VISITNUM in TV are the valid values for planned visits. Any VISITNUM appearing in subject-level datasets that is **not** in TV is assumed to correspond to an **unplanned visit**.

[Source: domains/TV/assumptions.md -- item_6]

### Handling Unplanned Visits

- **VISITNUM** should generally be populated even for unplanned visits (a missing VISITNUM is less useful). A common approach is to assign a generic value (e.g., 99) to all unplanned visits, though this sacrifices chronological sorting.
- **VISIT** may be left null or populated with a generic value (e.g., "Unscheduled").
- **VISITDY must NOT be populated** for unplanned visits — it is by definition the *planned* study day. The actual study day of an unplanned visit belongs in a `--DY` variable.

[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.5 Clinical Encounters and Visits]

---

## 2. The SV Domain's Role in Tracking Actual Visit Dates

### Structure and Purpose

**SV (Subject Visits)** is a **Special-Purpose** domain with the structure: *one record per actual or planned visit per subject*.

Its primary purpose is to provide reviewers with a **summary of a subject's actual visits** over the course of their participation. Key uses include:

- Comparing an individual subject's SV records against the TV dataset to **identify planned but not completed visits**.
- Comparing SVSTDY/SVENDY against VISIT/VISITDY to **highlight departures from planned visit timing**.

[Source: domains/SV/assumptions.md -- overview], [Source: model/03_special_purpose_domains.md -- Subject Visits (SV)]

### Key Variables

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core | CT |
|----------|-------|------|------|------|----|
| VISITNUM | Visit Number | Num | Topic | Req | — |
| VISIT | Visit Name | Char | Synonym Qualifier | — | — |
| SVSTDTC | Start Date/Time of Visit | Char | Timing | Exp | ISO 8601 |
| SVENDTC | End Date/Time of Visit | Char | Timing | Exp | ISO 8601 |
| SVSTDY | Study Day of Start of Visit | Num | Timing | Perm | — |
| SVENDY | Study Day of End of Visit | Num | Timing | Perm | — |
| SVUPDES | Description of Unplanned Visit | Char | Record Qualifier | Perm | — |
| SVPRESP | Pre-Specified | Char | Variable Qualifier | Exp | C66742 |
| SVOCCUR | Occurrence | Char | Record Qualifier | Exp | C66742 |
| SVCNTMOD | Contact Mode | Char | Record Qualifier | Perm | C171445 |
| SVEPCHGI | Epi/Pandemic Related Change Indicator | Char | Record Qualifier | Perm | C66742 |

[Source: model/03_special_purpose_domains.md -- Subject Visits (SV)], [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- SV]

Notably, **VISITNUM is the Topic variable** in SV (Role: Topic, Core: Req), whereas in observation-class domains it serves as a Timing variable. This reflects SV's role as the authoritative record of visit occurrences.

[Source: domains/SV/spec.md -- VISITNUM]

### Unplanned Visits in SV

Records for unplanned visits **must** be included in SV. The rule is:

> "The encounter should generally be treated as a visit if data from the encounter are included in any domain for which VISITNUM is included; a record with a missing value for VISITNUM is generally less useful than a record with VISITNUM populated. If the occasion is considered a visit, its date/times must be included in the SV table and a value of VISITNUM must be assigned."

SVUPDES can be populated with a description of the reason for the unplanned visit.

[Source: domains/SV/assumptions.md -- item_6]

---

## 3. Summary: How SV Anchors Visit Consistency

```
TV (Trial Visits)          ←→   SV (Subject Visits)
Planned VISITNUM/VISIT           Actual SVSTDTC/SVENDTC
Planned VISITDY                  Actual SVSTDY/SVENDY
                                 SVUPDES for unplanned
         ↓                              ↓
  Observation-class domains (LB, VS, AE, CM, etc.)
  carry VISITNUM/VISIT as Timing variables,
  values must match TV for planned visits
```

The SV domain thus serves as the **bridge between the planned visit schedule (TV) and the actual timing of data collection** recorded in observation-class domains, enabling reviewers to reconcile planned versus actual visit conduct at the subject level.

# RELSPEC Domain: Purpose, Structure, and Contrast with RELREC

## What is RELSPEC?

RELSPEC (Related Specimens) is a **Relationship-class dataset** introduced in SDTM v2.0 (and first included in SDTMIG v3.4). Its sole purpose is to describe **specimen lineage** — the genealogical relationships between biological specimens (e.g., a parent specimen and its derived aliquots or processed sub-specimens).

[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md]

---

## RELSPEC Variable Specification

| # | Variable | Label | Type | Role | Notes |
|---|----------|-------|------|------|-------|
| 1 | STUDYID | Study Identifier | Char | Identifier | |
| 2 | USUBJID | Unique Subject Identifier | Char | Identifier | |
| 3 | REFID | Reference ID | Char | Identifier | |
| 4 | SPEC | Specimen Type | Char | Variable Qualifier (REFID) | |
| 5 | PARENT | Specimen Parent | Char | Identifier | Identifies the REFID of the parent specimen to support tracking its genealogy |
| 6 | LEVEL | Specimen Level | Num | Variable Qualifier (REFID) | Identifies the generation number of the sample; the collected sample is considered the first generation |

[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md]

Three CDISC controlled terminology codelists may be applicable to SPEC: SPEC (C77529), SPECTYPE (C78734), and GENSMP (C111114). Sponsors are responsible for determining the most appropriate codelist(s).

[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md]

---

## Key Governing Assumptions

RELSPEC has two critical scoping constraints that sharply distinguish it from RELREC:

1. **RELSPEC is not used to manage relationships between any other datasets or domains.** It is exclusively a specimen-to-specimen relationship tool.
2. **RELSPEC is only used to maintain relationships between specimens**, and therefore does not require the additional variables used in RELREC (e.g., RDOMAIN, IDVAR, IDVARVAL, RELTYPE, RELID).

[Source: domains/RELSPEC/assumptions.md]

---

## Contrast: RELSPEC vs. RELREC

| Dimension | RELSPEC | RELREC |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| **Scope** | Specimen-to-specimen lineage only | Records within/across domains, or entire datasets |
| **Granularity** | Subject-level specimen hierarchy | Individual records, groups of records, or dataset-level |
| **Relationship mechanism** | PARENT variable points to the REFID of the parent specimen | RELID groups related records; IDVAR/IDVARVAL identify the specific record(s) |
| **Dataset-level linking** | **Not applicable** — cannot link datasets | Yes — RELTYPE (ONE/MANY) defines hierarchical dataset relationships |
| **Key variables** | REFID, PARENT, LEVEL | RDOMAIN, IDVAR, IDVARVAL, RELTYPE, RELID |
| **Cross-domain use** | No | Yes |

[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md; domains/RELSPEC/assumptions.md; chapters/ch08_relationships.md]

---

## Critical Point: RELSPEC Does NOT Define Study-Level Dataset Relationships

Your question asks about "relationships between datasets at the study level." This is **exclusively the role of RELREC**, not RELSPEC.

RELREC supports dataset-level relationships by:
- Including **one record per related dataset** (USUBJID and IDVARVAL are null for dataset-level relationships)
- Using **RELTYPE** = "ONE" or "MANY" to define the hierarchical nature of the join
- Using **IDVAR** to specify the key variable (e.g., TULNKID, TRLNKID) used to merge/join the two datasets

**Example** (TU → TR one-to-many dataset relationship):

| STUDYID | RDOMAIN | USUBJID | IDVAR | IDVARVAL | RELTYPE | RELID |
|---------|---------|---------|-------|----------|---------|-------|
| EFC1234 | TU | | TULNKID | | ONE | 1 |
| EFC1234 | TR | | TRLNKID | | MANY | 1 |

[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md]

RELSPEC has no equivalent capability — it operates strictly within the specimen hierarchy of a single subject, using the PARENT variable to chain REFID values across generations (LEVEL 1 = collected specimen, LEVEL 2 = first-generation derivative, etc.).

[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md]

results.answer:
## The Three General Observation Classes in the SDTM Model

The SDTM model organizes the majority of study observations into **3 general observation classes**:

### 1. Interventions
Represents investigational, therapeutic, and other treatments that are administered to or used by a subject, with some actual or expected physiological effect. This includes treatments specified by the study protocol (i.e., "exposure").

> *"An intervention is something that is done to a subject (possibly by the subject) that is expected to have a physiological effect."*

[Source: model/02_observation_classes.md -- 3.1.1 The Interventions Observation Class]

### 2. Events
Represents occurrences or incidents that happen to a subject spontaneously. Most events data captured in clinical trials concerns medical events (e.g., adverse events, medical history).

> *"An event is something that happens to a subject spontaneously."*

[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.6.1 Guidelines for Determining the General Observation Class]

### 3. Findings
Represents measurements, tests, assessments, or examinations performed on a subject in the clinical trial. These may be performed on the subject as a whole (e.g., height, heart rate) or on a specimen taken from a subject (e.g., blood sample, ECG tracing, tissue sample).

[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.6.1 Guidelines for Determining the General Observation Class]

---

### Key Points

- Domains based on these three classes share a common set of **Identifier** and **Timing** variables. [Source: model/02_observation_classes.md -- Overview]
- Within each class, variables must be ordered: **Identifiers → Topic → Qualifier → Timing**. [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.1.4 Order of the Variables]
- A subtype of Findings exists: **Findings About Events or Interventions** (FA domain). [Source: model/01_concepts_and_terms.md]
- These three classes are distinct from **Special-Purpose Domains** (e.g., DM, CO, SE) and **Trial Design Datasets**. [Source: model/02_observation_classes.md -- Overview]

results.answer:
# SDTM Core Designations: Req, Exp, and Perm

The Core column in SDTM domain specifications uses three designations to indicate how variables must be handled in a dataset submission.

---

## Summary Table

| Core Value | Full Name | Inclusion Rule | Null Allowed? |
|------------|-----------|----------------|---------------|
| **Req** | Required | Must always be included | **Never** — cannot be null for any record |
| **Exp** | Expected | Must always be included | Yes — when data not collected/applicable |
| **Perm** | Permissible | Include only if data collected | Yes — even if null, once included |

---

## Detailed Definitions

### Req (Required)
> "A Required variable is any variable that is basic to the identification of a data record (i.e., essential key variables and a topic variable) or is necessary to make the record meaningful. Required variables must always be included in the dataset and **cannot be null for any record**."

These are typically Identifier variables (e.g., STUDYID, USUBJID, --SEQ) and Topic variables (e.g., AETERM, VSTESTCD).

### Exp (Expected)
> "An Expected variable is any variable necessary to make a record useful in the context of a specific domain. Expected variables may contain some null values, but in most cases will not contain null values for every record."

Key rules for Exp variables:
- The **column must always be present** in the dataset
- Values should be populated when available
- If the study does not collect the data item at all, a **null column must still be included**, and a **comment must be added in the Define-XML document** stating that the study does not include the data item

### Perm (Permissible)
> "May be included in the dataset."

Key rules for Perm variables:
- **If the study collects the data** → the variable **must** be included in the dataset (even if some values are null) and **must** be declared in Define-XML
- **If the study did not collect the data** → the variable **should not** be included in the dataset and **should not** be declared in Define-XML
- Domain assumptions stating a Permissible variable is "generally not used" do **not** prohibit its use

---

## Additional Notes

- All identifier, timing, and general observation class variables not explicitly listed in a domain specification table are **Permissible** by default, unless specifically restricted by the SDTMIG (Section 2.7) or domain-specific assumptions.
- A null value is **implied** for any list of controlled terms unless the variable is Required.

[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.1.5 SDTM Core Designations]
